items.title: Here's what happened in crypto today
items.sum: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: Binance France emails announce closure of its users' accounts on Dec. 31
items.sum: Any assets left on the exchange will be charged monthly fees starting on Nov. 29, company says.

items.title: Amsterdam protesters break into Microsoft data center construction site: Report
items.sum: Dutch police said they detained 150-200 people for trespassing during the protest.

items.title: Binance's  finance chief Kaiser Ng to leave company, report says
items.sum: Ng will be replaced by Justin Yek, who was formerly vice-president of finance at Airwallex.

items.title: Ex-FBI counterintelligence agent stole almost $2.5M in crypto
items.sum: Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard.

items.title: Bitcoin holders have received eCash - What can you do with it?
items.sum: Bitcoin's eCash fork gives eligible holders an equivalent balance of ECX, but questions remain over where they can trade the tokens and what they can do with them.

items.title: This Bitcoin Developer's Idea Would Make Quantum Attacks a Losing Bet
items.sum: Cory Fields wants future quantum attackers to post Bitcoin as collateral before touching vulnerable wallets, giving prepared owners a chance to recover their coins and collect a potentially costly penalty.

items.title: Apple Completes the Set: Every Magnificent Seven Stock Opts Out of OKX-ICE Venue
items.sum: Apple and Meta's objections mean all seven of the biggest U.S. tech companies have now asked to keep their shares off the planned OKX-ICE venue.

items.title: AI Chip Stocks Bounce After Global Rout-But Is the Bubble Starting to Burst?
items.sum: A Friday rebound offered relief after a historic selloff. The question now is whether politics and mounting debt could turn an AI correction into something much worse.

items.title: Sony Axing Game Discs Will Have Outsized Impact on Low-Income Gamers, Experts Say
items.sum: Experts say a disc-free PlayStation will price out low-income players, while in much of Africa, digital-only gaming means breaking Sony's rules.

items.title: Treasury Cuts Crypto Exchange MEXC Off From US Financial System
items.sum: FinCEN's order, part of Operation Economic Outcast, bars U.S. institutions from any transfers to or from MEXC, which Treasury says facilitated $16 billion in illicit finance tied to Iran, North Korea and Russia.

items.title: Greece Passes Crypto Tax Law With 10% Gains Levy, 15% on Staking and DeFi
items.sum: Greece has approved a crypto tax framework with a 500 ($557) annual gains threshold and new rules for staking and DeFi income, but lawmakers left important questions about token swaps unresolved.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin says ETH should be valued as a store of value, not a fee-burning token
items.sum: A recent controversial proposal to burn a rising share of validator rewards as more ETH is staked was withdrawn last month after facing pushback.

items.title: Binance CFO steps down nine days after record hack; co-CEO says transition was planned six months ago
items.sum: Co-CEO Yi He said Ng is departing to pursue a new venture, under a transition plan put in place over the past six months.

items.title: Ex-FBI agent pleads guilty to stealing $2.47 million in crypto from wallets tied to 35 investigations
items.sum: Yaroch will pay at least $2.4 million in restitution and will forfeit any profits he would earn in the future from telling his story.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs flip negative for 2026 after $1.28 billion outflow week, worst since June
items.sum: BlackRock's IBIT accounted for 98% of Friday's outflows, with $403 million leaving the industry-leading fund.

items.title: Treasury cuts off MEXC Global over alleged $16 billion in transactions linked to Iran, North Korea and Russia
items.sum: Treasury says it has severed MEXC Global from the U.S. after it allegedly supported $16 billion in transactions connected to Iran.

items.title: US Treasury walks back crypto surveillance 'travel rule' proposal
items.sum: The Treasury Department has withdrawn a controversial proposal that would have expanded requirements for cryptocurrency transactions.

items.title: One BlackRock fund dominates Bitcoin's billion-dollar ETF exodus
items.sum: Fidelity finished positive in the November 2-6 week, but the other funds collectively remained negative without IBIT.

items.title: Nvidia's CEO, an alleged romance and a suspected Chinese spy: Congress wants answers
items.sum: The reported intelligence memo adds detail to an earlier House briefing request, with an answer sought by November 11.

items.title: A single AI forecast inflates US power auctions by $5.7B
items.sum: Australia's latest inflation figures showed that prices in the category covering audio, visual, and computing equipment rose 6.1% in a single quarter.

items.title: Gold is still 25% below its peak even as demand reaches $188B in Q3
items.sum: Central banks bought more gold in the third quarter of 2026 than consumers worldwide bought for jewelry.

items.title: Thailand is cutting off Bitget. Users have until December 5 to prepare
items.sum: The regulator asks customers to consider action on holdings before the block, while Bitget promises guidance on service access.

items.title: US sanctions hit 41 companies accused of keeping Prince Group's scam network running
items.sum: Treasury says the network concealed ownership and sustained Prince Group operations, while US rules require covered assets to be blocked.
